title: Access & roles
summary: Firm roles, a per-capability permission matrix, matter-level teams, restricted matters and ethical walls, and separation of duties. Running the system and seeing client confidences are different powers: the system administrator cannot open matter content or move trust money. Approvals are always by someone other than the maker, and the agent never approves.

sod: No one approves, authorizes or signs off an item they created, edited or requested; the agent counts as the human it acted for.
The agent never approves, authorizes, executes trust payments, changes access or lifts walls.
The system administrator cannot open matter content, see billing or trust amounts, use break-glass, or approve any gate.
No one can change their own role, grants, team membership or wall status.
Trust withdrawals and transfers are authorized only by a designated licensee signatory who is not the requester.
The person who executes a trust payment at the bank is not the person who authorized it (where the firm has two people).
Bookkeeper prepares reconciliations; a licensee signatory signs them off.
Trust signatories are added only by an owner who already holds signing authority.
Bills are approved by a lawyer, not by the bookkeeper who prepared them; write-offs approved by a lawyer other than the requester.
Wall lifts need a lawyer who is neither screened nor the requester.
Break-glass use is reviewed by a different owner; break-glass never allows money or access changes.
Access reviews are certified by someone other than the person reviewed.
Read-only auditor access always has an expiry.
Sole practitioner: self-approval is allowed only as a declared, logged exception with a cooling-off delay on trust and export actions.
MFA resets and authority-limit changes are approved by someone other than the person affected.
Vendor support never holds standing access; each grant is owner-approved, scoped, time-limited and logged.

clio_compare.clio: One administrator role holds every right: settings, users, firm data, and bank and trust account powers the firm cannot switch off. An admin can be left off a matter's permission list but can still list such matters and bulk-change their permissions, so can re-grant themselves any matter.
clio_compare.ours: Split system admin (runs the system, names only) from firm owner (licensee). Admin cannot read privileged content or move money; firm owners are bound by walls too.

clio_compare.clio: Every user holds one or more roles (most permissive wins). Five built-in roles act as templates; custom roles toggle per-area permissions and are a top-tier feature (CA: Signature/Elite unlimited, a small cap on Core; none on Starter). Timekeeping scope is all / accessible matters / own.
clio_compare.ours: One capability matrix with five levels (none, view, own, all, approve) per capability, so scope and approval power are explicit.

clio_compare.clio: Users with the reports permission see the firm dashboard and productivity reports for colleagues; whether rates leak this way is unproven (verify), since the detailed annual report also needs billing permission and unrestricted rate visibility.
clio_compare.ours: Reports inherit the underlying capability; a user only sees figures they could see on the source screens.

clio_compare.clio: Firm-wide activity feed visible to administrators by default; others need a custom role permission (help.clio.com/hc/articles/9200279456667).
clio_compare.ours: Access audit log shows metadata only; restricted matter names hidden from the admin; reading the log is itself logged.

clio_compare.clio: Matters open to everyone by default; can be limited to specific users or groups, at most 20 entries combined; any user can set it while creating or editing a matter.
clio_compare.ours: Three modes (firm-open, team-only, restricted) set at opening, with responsible-lawyer approval; no cap on team size.

clio_compare.clio: Done by blocking users from matters, one at a time or in bulk.
clio_compare.ours: Walls are first-class records created from conflict clearance, with undertakings, effective date proof and nightly enforcement tests, including against the agent.

clio_compare.clio: Accounts permission covers bank and trust accounts; trust request flows exist but signing authority is not tied to licence status.
clio_compare.ours: Request, authorize, execute and sign-off are separate capabilities; authorize needs a designated licensee signatory, and requester cannot authorize.

clio_compare.clio: Portal access shared per matter with contacts; firm chooses what to share.
clio_compare.ours: Same idea, plus client role cannot see anything not explicitly released through a documents.release gate.

clio_compare.clio: Grow users are Normal or Admin, separate from Manage roles; the newer Admin Console manages users, roles and licences across products, and Manage licence changes mirror to Grow.
clio_compare.ours: One role model across intake and matters, so a person has one set of rights.

clio_compare.clio: Third-party apps use OAuth 2.0 authorization code; access is the app's scopes combined with the authorizing user's own role permissions.
clio_compare.ours: Integrations act under a service identity with a named capability set and never above the connecting admin; the agent runs as the requesting human, reduced by its own column.

clio_compare.clio: No logged emergency access or periodic access certification found; an admin can simply re-grant themselves any matter.
clio_compare.ours: Break-glass with mandatory after-review, and quarterly access reviews.

clio_compare.clio: Per-user setting (all, own, none) for whose hourly rates show when entering time; set by admins.
clio_compare.ours: rates.view is a capability in the matrix (none, own, all) and every report and screen honours it, so rates never leak through reports.

clio_compare.clio: Deactivate keeps history; Reassign Work moves tasks (sources differ on matters and events) from open matters only; closed-matter work cannot move; licence stays billed until removed.
clio_compare.ours: Offboard wizard inventories matters (open and closed), work, time, events and signatory status; agent proposes successors; responsible lawyers approve handovers; cut-off ends sessions and tokens at once.

clio_compare.clio: MFA administered per user and mandatory from January 2026 per help text; SAML SSO with domain verification on top tiers; login activity and device sessions with forced logout; email on unrecognised device.
clio_compare.ours: MFA mandatory with passkey or TOTP from day one; OIDC SSO first, SAML later; idle timeout, lockout and optional IP list; all changes owner-approved; firm-wide Sign-ins tab in the access audit.

clio_compare.clio: Support needs explicit in-app permission from the firm for temporary, logged, revocable data access.
clio_compare.ours: Same principle, plus scope levels (settings, matter metadata, matter content), walled matters excluded, owner-only grant, and an agent summary of every support session.

clio_compare.clio: Admin-defined groups used for matter permissions, calendar sharing and client rates; archiving a group leaves it on matters, calendars and rates.
clio_compare.ours: Teams work the same way, but archiving forces a replacement wherever the team is used.

clio_compare.clio: Not found in Manage; Clio Operate (enterprise) ties approvals to competencies and authority limits.
clio_compare.ours: Per-person authority limits (write-down %, trust withdrawal amount, practice areas) checked by gates in addition to role.

roles.name: Firm owner
roles.desc: Licensee who owns or manages the firm. Holds final approval for roles, signatories, rule packs and retention. Sees all matters except those walled off from them. Two owners are recommended so no owner approves their own access.

roles.name: System administrator
roles.desc: Runs the system: users, sign-in and security, integrations, templates, automation settings. Sees matter names and numbers only. Cannot open matter content, see billing or trust figures, or approve anything that grants access.

roles.name: Lawyer (responsible)
roles.desc: Licensed lawyer who can be responsible lawyer on matters. Sees all non-restricted matters, approves engagement, clearance, bills, deadlines and, if designated, trust withdrawals.

roles.name: Associate
roles.desc: Licensed lawyer working on matters they are on the team for. Approves deadlines and documents on those matters; cannot approve bills, trust or firm settings by default.

roles.name: Paralegal (licensee)
roles.desc: LSO-licensed paralegal. Works team matters within their licensed scope; can do second checks on deadlines; cannot give final approval on matters outside paralegal scope (verify scope per practice area).

roles.name: Law clerk / assistant
roles.desc: Non-licensee staff working team matters under a named supervising licensee. Prepares and drafts; never approves; work going to a client goes through a licensee gate.

roles.name: Bookkeeper
roles.desc: Keeps books: time review, bills, payments, trust postings and reconciliations. Can execute an authorized trust payment at the bank if bonded and given signing authority (verify). Never authorizes trust withdrawals or signs off a reconciliation.

roles.name: Read-only auditor
roles.desc: Time-boxed, read-only access for an external accountant, LSO spot auditor or internal compliance reviewer. Sees financial records, registers and audit logs. No matter documents unless an owner grants a named matter.

roles.name: Client (portal)
roles.desc: External person with portal access to their own matters only: shared documents, invoices, trust balance, messages, signing and ID checks.

roles.name: Agent
roles.desc: The AI agent. Acts only inside the scope of the job or the human who asked it, and only on matters that human can see. Drafts, matches, checks. Never approves, never authorizes money, never changes access.

levels.own: only matters the user is on the team for, or items assigned to them
levels.all: every matter the user is not walled off from
levels.approve: all, plus eligible to approve the gate (never their own item; trust also needs signatory designation)

capabilities.name: Convert lead to matter / approve engagement
Create or lift an ethical wall
See matter names and numbers (no content)
Change a matter's team and access
Release a document or agent draft to a client or other side
Write down or write off time
Request a trust withdrawal or transfer
Authorize trust withdrawal or transfer (designated signatory only)
Execute an authorized payment at the bank
Share to and message in the client portal
Ask the agent to do work
Sign-in, SSO, MFA, sessions, IP limits
Offboard a person and hand over their work

open_questions: Does this area replace platform/users-roles, or does users-roles stay as a summary linking here?
May a licensed paralegal hold trust signing authority in our product, or lawyers only? (BL9 allows licensees, verify)
Should bonded non-licensee bookkeepers be allowed to execute EFTs, or execution limited to licensees?
Dual-authorization threshold for trust withdrawals: off by default, or on above an amount?
Sole practitioners: accept declared self-approval with cooling-off delay, or require an outside reviewer?
Should firm owners be able to see restricted matters they are not on, or must they use break-glass?
Auditor access to matter documents: never, or named matters with owner grant?
Is a custom role builder needed at launch, or built-in roles plus temporary grants?
Multiple roles per user (Clio: most permissive wins): keep one role plus temporary grants, or allow several roles later?
Seat counter on user-list: show seats in use only, or nothing, given per-firm pricing?
Sole owner MFA recovery: what identity check and delay do we accept?
Should the support-access content scope exist at all, or settings and metadata only?
